findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Rewrite the Linux collect-only verification so that each .args file is passed as its own `@` argument (or move the check into the pin test), instead of a glob prefixed with `@`.
evidence: Plan: "`pytest --collect-only -m \"not integration and not external\" @.github/windows-sweep-deselect/*.args` on Linux collects without error"
findings.finding: The Linux verification command `pytest --collect-only ... @.github/windows-sweep-deselect/*.args` does not work as written. The shell glob begins with a literal `@`, so it matches no file, and pytest receives the single argument `@.github/windows-sweep-deselect/*.args` and tries to open a file named `*.args`. The check the plan relies on to prove 'none is a silent no-op' therefore cannot run as stated.
findings.location: Testing (second bullet)
scenarios: An implementer runs the command exactly as written, gets a file-not-found error, and either skips the check or misreads the error.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `pytest --collect-only -q -m "not integration and not external" $(printf '@%s ' .github/windows-sweep-deselect/*.args)`, or have tests/unit/test_windows_sweep_deselect.py build the argument list from the files and run the collection itself.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Rewrite the Linux collect-only check so each `.args` file is passed as its own `@<path>` argument (expand the glob first, then add the `@`), and re-confirm the 917-id match with the corrected command.
evidence: Plan quote: "`pytest --collect-only -m \"not integration and not external\" @.github/windows-sweep-deselect/*.args` on Linux collects without error."
Shell semantics: a glob pattern matches whole pathnames, so the `@` prefix makes the pattern unmatchable and bash leaves the word unexpanded.
Evidence class: Contradicted (POSIX shell behaviour rules out the command as written).
findings.finding: The Linux check command in Testing, `pytest --collect-only -m "not integration and not external" @.github/windows-sweep-deselect/*.args`, does not work as written. Bash glob-expands the whole word, which starts with a literal `@`, and no path starts with `@.github/`. With no match (and nullglob off), bash passes the literal string `@.github/windows-sweep-deselect/*.args` to pytest. argparse then tries to open a file literally named `.github/windows-sweep-deselect/*.args` and exits with 'No such file or directory'. So the claim that 'All 917 --deselect ids match a collected node id' cannot have come from this command.
findings.location: Testing — second bullet (`pytest --collect-only ... @.github/windows-sweep-deselect/*.args`)
scenarios: A reviewer or CI author copies the command to re-check that no deselect is a no-op, gets an argparse file-not-found error, and either drops the check or mistakes it for a pytest problem.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `pytest --collect-only -q -m "not integration and not external" $(for f in .github/windows-sweep-deselect/*.args; do printf '@%s ' "$f"; done)`, or the bash expansion `"${files[@]/#/@}"` after `files=(.github/windows-sweep-deselect/*.args)`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either make the Linux pin test assert every `--deselect` id resolves to a collected node id (and add a shrink-only guard, e.g. a committed per-file line-count ceiling), or drop the 'cannot leave a dead entry' / 'only shrinks' claims.

'Fixing a class deletes its lines (and its file once empty), so the list only shrinks.'
findings.finding: Two guarantees are claimed but not enforced by the pin test. (1) 'a rename cannot leave a dead entry': the test only checks that the listed module exists. A test function renamed or moved within an existing module leaves a `--deselect` that pytest silently ignores. The Testing note that all 917 ids match collected nodes is a one-time manual check. (2) 'the list only shrinks': nothing stops a contributor from appending a new `--deselect` line to hide a fresh Windows regression. A deselected test that becomes fixed incidentally also stays hidden forever.
findings.location: Approach — unit test bullet ('every listed module still exists so a rename cannot leave a dead entry'); 'so the list only shrinks'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the pin test (or the Linux collect-only check) assert that each `--deselect` id matches EXACTLY the intended collected node ids. Fail when the id is a strict prefix of any other collected node id, and require that the deselected count equals the number of listed ids.
evidence: Plan: "each line `--deselect=<nodeid>`"
Plan: "All 917 `--deselect` ids match a collected node id, so none is a silent no-op."
pytest main.py deselect_by_prefix: `if colitem.nodeid.startswith(deselect_prefixes)`
findings.finding: pytest's `--deselect` matches node ids by PREFIX (`colitem.nodeid.startswith(deselect_prefixes)`), not exact equality. A line like `--deselect=tests/unit/test_x.py::test_lock` therefore also deselects `test_lock_release`, `test_lock[param]` and every other test whose id starts with that string, including tests that pass on Windows. The planned check that 'all 917 --deselect ids match a collected node id' only finds dead entries. It cannot find over-matching, so the maintained subset can be silently smaller than intended, and regressions in the extra hidden tests stay invisible.
findings.location: Approach (`--deselect=<nodeid>` lines) / Testing ('All 917 --deselect ids match a collected node id')
scenarios: A deselect for a non-parametrized `test_foo` also removes a passing `test_foo_windows_path` from the Windows run.
A deselect for one bad parametrize case without its full bracket id removes every case of that test.
findings.suggested_fix: In tests/unit/test_windows_sweep_deselect.py (or the collect-only verification), collect node ids and, for each listed id, assert `[n for n in collected if n.startswith(id)] == [id]`. Also check that the `N deselected` count reported by `--collect-only` equals the number of `--deselect` lines.

The claim that 'Fixing a class deletes its lines … so the list only shrinks' depends entirely on the fixer remembering to edit the file. A test fixed by accident, or by an unrelated change, stays deselected forever. The plan's 'module still exists' check catches renames, not fixes. The stale part of the list then grows and permanently removes coverage the advisory job could have regained.

The AC 'a NEW regression would be visible' therefore has no proof that can actually fail.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Provide a CI-independent entry point for the Windows subset (e.g. a make target or a documented per-file `@` invocation that works in PowerShell) and have the pin test reference it rather than only the workflow command.

'`pytest --collect-only -m "not integration and not external" @.github/windows-sweep-deselect/*.args` on Linux'

findings.finding: The maintained-subset contract exists only inside the GitHub Actions step command. The pin test enforces that the files are wired into 'the command and nothing else'. The only documented invocation, `@.github/windows-sweep-deselect/*.args`, relies on POSIX shell glob expansion. findings.finding: The plan's capability claim that pytest reads `@file` natively is true only from pytest 8.2.0, but the repo declares `pytest>=8`. Nothing in the plan raises that floor or records the 8.2 requirement. On pytest 8.0 or 8.1, `@.github/windows-sweep-deselect/<class>.args` is not expanded and is treated as a positional path, so the run fails with 'file or directory not found' instead of deselecting anything.
findings.location: Approach — "pytest's argument parser reads `@file` natively (`fromfile_prefix_chars="@"`)"; pyproject.toml line 245
scenarios: A user, or the `sweep (declared lower-bound resolution)` job, resolves pytest 8.0/8.1. Any invocation that passes the `.args` files, such as the plan's Linux `--collect-only @...` check, then errors instead of deselecting.

A future constraint or cached resolver result pins pytest below 8.2 on the Windows runner. The sweep goes red for a reason that has nothing to do with a Windows regression, which is exactly the signal loss this ticket is fixing.
findings.suggested_fix: Change pyproject.toml's dev dependency to `"pytest>=8.2,!=9.1.0,!=9.1.1"` and add a comment citing pytest #11871 (`@file` argument files, 8.2.0). Then add `pyproject.toml` to the plan's Scope list.

findings.finding: The plan says pytest's argument parser reads `@file` natively, but gives no version. My recollection, not observed here, is that this arrived in pytest 8.2.0 (changelog #11871). The declared dependency is `pytest>=8,!=9.1.0,!=9.1.1`, which allows 8.0/8.1, where an `@path` token would be treated as a positional test path, not an argument file. The Windows job installs unlocked, so whatever pytest it resolves is the only thing that keeps the integration working. The `sweep (declared lower-bound resolution)` job runs `tests/unit` against `--resolution lowest-direct`, so it would hit any part of the new unit test that calls pytest with `@` arguments.
findings.location: Approach — first bullet ("pytest's argument parser reads `@file` natively"); pyproject.toml:245 `pytest>=8,!=9.1.0,!=9.1.1`
scenarios: A resolver or environment picks pytest 8.0/8.1 for the Windows job: `@...args` is treated as a missing test path, collection errors or the deselects are ignored, and the sweep goes red for reasons unrelated to Windows.
The new unit test (or a later version of it) shells out to `pytest --collect-only @...` and fails in the lower-bound sweep on pytest 8.0.
